meta.siteDescription: AI/ML Engineer and Full-Stack Developer. Portfolio of Marshall Rasendria Mahendra, styled as a living Word document.

paragraphs: I build AI systems end to end, from training deep learning and computer vision models to RAG pipelines on vector databases, then ship them inside full-stack platforms deployed with Docker and Kubernetes. Information Systems undergraduate at Telkom University, currently interning as an AI Engineer, and permanently curious.

Three AI engineering internships so far, across enterprise document automation, cloud data workflows, and medical imaging research. AWS Certified AI Practitioner and Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals among 6 professional certifications, plus a first-author publication, 6+ shipped end-to-end products, and national finalist placements in 3 hackathons. I like my evaluation leakage-free, my answers cited, and my coffee unsupervised.
This whole site is one big document. Go ahead, switch to Editing mode and mess with it. It resets when you refresh, just like my sleep schedule.

Engineered the PDF system end to end on dompdf, with pixel-accurate official templates, a two-pass render that fills the table of contents with real page numbers, FPDI merging of uploaded attachments, and render caching. Closed all 9 findings from the PuTI Directorate's vulnerability assessment and locked each fix with regression tests, covering a nonce-based strict CSP, owner-only authorization, HTMLPurifier sanitization, private file storage, and layered rate limiting.

Delivered AI/ML solutions for an enterprise client as part of the outsourced engineering team, working across the full model development lifecycle on Google Cloud Platform with BigQuery for large-scale data processing.

Medical imaging research on mammography classification. Built reproducible, patient-level-split pipelines on CBIS-DDSM and trained six deep learning architectures across whole-image and lesion-region inputs, from hybrid attention to mammography foundation models. The work became a first-author journal article in JADIMI.

Led backend development of a campus service marketplace built with UKM CSC on a 6-person team. Designed the architecture and a 20-model PostgreSQL schema from scratch with NestJS and Prisma, built every backend module across 90+ REST endpoints, developed the Midtrans payment system with SHA-512 webhook verification, merchant withdrawals, and monthly revenue-sharing reports, and added real-time user-to-merchant chat with Stream Chat.
B2B outreach for a national sports event. Approached 40+ corporate sponsors across 15+ pitching sessions, reaching a 90 percent sponsorship slot fulfilment rate before competition day.

projects.name: GAP
projects.tagline: RAG-powered API intelligence and gap analysis platform
points: Scans a codebase from a GitHub URL or dropped folder, detects backend routes across Express, FastAPI, Laravel, NestJS, and Next.js and frontend calls across fetch, axios, and React Query, then flags connected, orphan, and ghost endpoints.

“Ask your codebase” RAG: route-handler chunks, overlapping 60-line windows, and per-route summary cards embedded with Gemini into pgvector behind an HNSW cosine index, retrieving the top 6 after similarity thresholding and overlap deduplication.

Answers are grounded strictly in the retrieved sources with inline citations to file paths, line ranges, and routes, and say so plainly instead of inventing endpoints when nothing relevant comes back.
Hybrid pipeline runs deterministic parsers first with LLM fallback, ships with Docker on Kubernetes, and is backed by 200+ Vitest tests.

faq.q: Why does your portfolio look like Microsoft Word?
faq.a: Because every portfolio looks the same, and nobody expects a resume that is literally a document you can poke at. Also, I spend half my life in documents anyway.

faq.q: Can I really edit this page?
faq.a: Yes. Switch to Editing mode at the top right, select some text, and go wild with the toolbar. Refresh the page and everything is back to normal. No commitment issues here.

faq.q: AI/ML or full-stack, which one are you really?
faq.a: Both, and that is the point. I train the model, then I build the product around it. A model without a product is a very expensive CSV file.

faq.q: What are you looking for right now?
faq.a: Interesting problems, good teams, and opportunities in AI/ML engineering or full-stack roles. If you have one of those, the comment section and my inbox are open.

faq.q: What is the most honest thing on this site?
faq.a: The research numbers. I spent a whole internship proving that most 99 percent accuracy claims in mammography papers come from data leakage. My 0.86 AUC is boring and real, and I am proud of it.

typing.intro: Each round is three IT sentences. Type them fast and clean, then claim your spot on the public leaderboard. One name per browser, best score counts.
sentences: There are only two hard things in computer science, cache invalidation and naming things.
It works on my machine is the start of every great debugging story.
Machine learning is just spicy statistics running on very expensive hardware.
A deployed model in production beats a perfect model in a notebook.
The best code review comment is a test case that proves the bug.
Never push to production on a Friday afternoon unless you enjoy weekend debugging.
Clean code always looks like it was written by someone who cares.
The database is always fine until the day you forget to back it up.
Every senior engineer was once a junior who refused to give up.
A good API is like a good joke, if you have to explain it, it is not that good.

publications.title: Controlled Comparison of Multimodal Hybrid Deep Learning for Benign-Malignant Mammogram Classification on CBIS-DDSM
publications.publisher: JADIMI: Journal of AI-Driven Informatics and Management Information
publications.authors: Marshall Rasendria Mahendra, Farhan Muamar Fawwaz, Naisya Aghis Nabila, Muhammad Rakha
publications.description: Many deep learning studies on CBIS-DDSM report accuracy above 95 percent, yet they partition the archive at image level, so views of one patient land in both the training and the test set and the figures cannot be trusted. This paper rebuilds the comparison honestly. Six models are trained on two image representations, the whole mammogram and the lesion region of interest, under one identical training recipe: EfficientNet-B3, ConvNeXt-Tiny, a gated hybrid fusion of the two with the Convolutional Block Attention Module, two variants that fuse seven clinical descriptors through a perceptron, and a Mammo-CLIP backbone pretrained on mammograms. The official CBIS-DDSM partition is enforced at patient level across 1,104 disjoint patients, and the BI-RADS assessment is dropped to avoid circular prediction. The strongest model, Hybrid Fusion with CBAM and clinical metadata, reaches an AUC of 0.856 on regions of interest and 0.845 on whole images. Clinical metadata is the largest single source of gain, close to six AUC points on both representations, and Grad-CAM shows attention settling on the lesion rather than on artifacts.
